newsitem.title: FRANCE: Utilities EDF, RWE take stakes in ATEL.
newsitem.headline: Utilities EDF, RWE take stakes in ATEL.

text.p: French utility EDF (Electricite de France) and RWE (Rheinisch-Westfaelische Elektrizitaetswerk AG) of Germany have agreed to buy 40 percent of the Swiss holding company controlling ATEL (Aare und Tessin Electricitaat) from Union Bank of Switzerland, EDF said on Saturday.
It said in a statement it would pay about one billion French francs for the investment in Motor Columbus, which controls ATEL, under an accord signed on Friday with RWE and UBS.
"Under the terms of the accord, the two electrical utilities will take 20 percent each of the capital of Swiss company Motor Columbus AG, with UBS retaining 35.6 percent," EDF said.
It said the deal strengthened its presence in Switzerland, its top export client, and formed the basis of an international partnership with RWE, Germany's leading utility.

Meanwhile in an interview published on Saturday by the newspaper Le Monde, EDF chairman Edmond Alphandery said,"This strategic acquisition...is part of a binding of ties among European electrical utilities."

European Union energy ministers agreed in June to open electricity markets to limited competition in phases. Under the accord, nearly a quarter of the EU market will be open from 1999 to competition from companies other than existing monopolies.
This will increase to nearly a third of the market by January 2003.

Alphandery said EDF was prepared for the liberalisation. "EDF is the biggest exporter in Europe and generates 15 percent of its turnover (from exports). The company doesn't need to worry but it needs to adapt itself," he was quoted as saying.

He said EDF had spent five billion francs in investments this year, more than the total spent in all the years since 1992. "We have also clarified our strategy by concentrating on three zones -- Europe, Latin America and Asia," he said.
Switzerland is pivotal for Europe, he added.
"ATEL alone controls nearly half of Swiss (electricity) exports. We are sealing not only our longstanding ties with this Swiss company but also with RWE, the German leader," he said.

ATEL represents eight percent of sales in Switzerland, 13 percent of production, 24 percent of domestic transport energy and 45 percent of sales abroad, EDF said. Its 1995 turnover was 1.65 billion Swiss francs, or 6.75 billion French francs.
EDF, whose 1995 turnover was 188.6 billion francs, said the deal would also give it greater access to markets in northern Italy, Germany, Austria and countries further east.
